subject: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval — next steps
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval — next steps

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap
- Acme Bio goal: deploy an LLM-powered internal R&D assistant with predictable latency and cost.
- Primary constraint: capacity guarantees for nightly large-batch workloads and priority for daytime inference spikes.
- Evaluation axis: 1) latency P50/P95, 2) cost per token at target throughput, 3) capacity predictability / reserved lanes, 4) operational controls (SLOs, routing, fallbacks).

Proposed next steps (POC plan)
1) POC: run a 2-week comparative evaluation — Redwood Dedicated vs Acme's preferred hyperscaler managed endpoints. We’ll run identical workloads and surface latency histograms, cost modeling, and failure-mode behavior.
2) Test plan: we’ll execute the attached Acme POC test plan (acme-poc-test-plan.xlsx). Key tests: steady 200 req/s baseline, day-spike simulation (3x baseline for 30 min), cold-start recovery, and long-seq generation load.
3) Capacity ask: if you confirm Reserved Capacity target (e.g., 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved with burst pool), we’ll provide a committed pricing option and an SLA for latency/uptime.
4) Deliverables: performance report, cost comparison, suggested config for Dedicated (batching/caching, quantization profile), and a draft SOW for committed capacity.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-overview.pdf, acme-poc-test-plan.xlsx, SOW-draft-Acme_v1.docx

Can you confirm the reserved capacity target (GPU-equivalent) you were thinking about and whether procurement should be looped in now or after performance validation?

If that looks right I’ll schedule the kickoff next week and loop in our solutions engineering lead (Rishi) for infra setup.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Thanks Markus — great summary. Confirming a few points and a couple questions from procurement below.

Quick answers:
- We’re thinking about reserving capacity equivalent to ~6-8 A100s for baseline, with a 2-3 GPU burst pool for spikes.
- Procurement would like a rough committed pricing band and an example SOW before they fully engage, but they’re happy for the SE team to run the tech POC first.

Procurement Qs:
- Do you offer monthly reserved commits or only annual?
- What guarantees are in the SLA for latency and capacity? We need something we can reference in our procurement doc.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood Dedicated supports rapid fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is briefly saturated (we need predictable availability during spikes)?

Appreciate it — if you can send those details we’ll confirm and get procurement on the thread as needed.

—Daniel
Daniel Evans
Head of AI Infrastructure | Acme Bio

Daniel — thanks for the quick reply and the capacity range, that’s helpful. Answers below and next steps.

Procurement / SLA / pricing
- Commits: we support monthly and annual reserved capacity contracts. Monthly is available for Enterprise customers with a short-term commitment; annual gives the best unit pricing and is what we recommend for predictable workload economics.
- SLA: for reserved capacity we can contract to an uptime SLA (e.g., 99.9%) and latency SLO bands per route/model. For POCs we usually provide a performance target and operational playbook; contractual SLAs kick in on committed contracts. I’ve attached a draft SOW with example SLA language.
- Fallbacks: Redwood Dedicated supports automated fallback routing to compatible hosted model variants or lower-cost model variants when Dedicated capacity is saturated. Fallback behavior is policy-driven — we can set hard reserve lanes for critical routes so you keep guaranteed throughput during spikes.

Proposed POC details (high level)
- Duration: 10 business days of steady comparative runs + a 2-day spike window.
- Tests: see attached spreadsheet — we will provide a reproducible workload generator and a Redwood config that mirrors your hyperscaler setup.
- Metrics: P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, token cost estimate, failure/retry rate, cold-start times, tail-latency histograms.

Action items
- Daniel: confirm final reserved GPU-equivalent number (6 vs 8) and whether procurement wants the SOW before or after POC.
- Rishi: can you validate infra onboarding steps and estimate time to provision a 6-A100 equivalent Dedicated pool (incl. burst config)?
- Lauren: can you draft two committed pricing options (monthly and annual) that map to 6-A100 and 8-A100 reserved options?

I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for next Tue to align on test tooling and infra. Proposed slot: Tue 2026-10-13 10:00 PT. 

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

Markus

Markus / Rishi —

Per the thread with Acme Bio, I drafted two pricing options for the 6-A100 and 8-A100 reserved capacity commitments. High level:

Option A (Monthly commit) — 6 A100-eq
- Unit price premium vs on-demand: ~18%
- Monthly minimum: $120k
- Includes burst pool up to 2 GPUs with priority queuing
- No long-term early termination fee (30-day notice)

Option B (Annual commit) — 8 A100-eq
- Unit price discount vs on-demand: ~27%
- Annual commitment: $1.2M (paid monthly or upfront)
- Includes burst pool up to 3 GPUs, 99.9% uptime SLA on reserved lanes, 5ms per-token P50 target (model dependent)
- Includes 8 hours of on-call SE support per month during ramp period

Notes / next steps:
- I left placeholders in the SOW for exact model family (we should mirror the model used in the POC).
- If Acme wants guaranteed latency bands in the contract we should lock in the test prompt set and sequence length distribution to make the SLOs measurable.
- Rishi: can you confirm provisioning lead time (ETA) so I can add to the SOW?

I’ll prepare a short comparison slide and a redlined SOW for procurement once Markus confirms which option Acme prefers.

—Lauren
